review_scope: Additive perf revision r2 on top of the already-APPROVED, MERGE-READY-on-correctness r1. Reviewed against the ACTUAL code in crates/axc-runtime/src/{buffers.rs,kernel_handle.rs,context.rs} and axc-hir/src/{param.rs,buffer.rs}. r1's correctness invariants (CRITICAL-1..6) are NOT re-litigated except where r2 touches them.
verified_against_code: BufferAccess enum (axc-hir/src/buffer.rs:17) has exactly ReadWrite/ReadOnly/WriteOnly; BufferBindingSlot.ty.access is reachable from inner.binding_plan.buffers[i] (param.rs:66-78, ParamBindingPlan.buffers). Lever A's predicate keyed on .ty.access is sound and the access classification is the one the descriptor decoration already uses (ReadOnly→NonWritable), so it matches the SPIR-V-level write capability.

Current readback gates are exactly the five the design enumerates: single-queue compute→transfer loop (kernel_handle.rs:772), single-queue Stage-B copy loop (:795), dedicated compute→transfer loop (:1071), dedicated readback-copy loop (:1104), and readback_from_persistent_mapping (:1455). All five gate on `output_sizes[i]==0` ONLY — confirming Lever A's claim that access mode is currently IGNORED for readback and that read-only inputs ARE needlessly copied back.

r1 ALREADY implements the submit-collapse machinery Lever B reuses: submit_compute has a `signal_fence_directly` param (kernel_handle.rs:1326,1329) and the dedicated path computes `readback_cb_opt.is_none()` (:1168) so that when has_outputs is false the COMPUTE submit signals inner.fence directly and the readback CB is skipped. r2's `has_staged_readback` is a strict generalization of the existing `has_outputs` gate — NOT a new branch. The error-recovery matrix (:1148-1222) already handles upload_cb_opt/readback_cb_opt being None at every failure point.

Drop (kernel_handle.rs:189-210) and grow (ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props :377-388) BOTH already do unmap-before-destroy-before-free for staging, consuming PersistentMapping by value so a forgotten unmap is a COMPILE error. Adding the same conditional `if let Some(m)=device_local.mapping.take()` unmap is a mechanical mirror of an already-proven pattern.

Descriptor write binds slot.device_local.buffer (kernel_handle.rs:441) — unchanged by Lever B; the ReBAR buffer is the SAME device_local.buffer, so the SSBO descriptor is correct with zero layout change.

find_device_local_memory_type_index (buffers.rs:559) already returns the DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE unified type for iGPU; allocate_device_local_buffer's iGPU fallback (:577) is independent of the ReBAR mapping decision (different buffers), so no aliasing.

force-option plumbing (context.rs:127 read_bool_flag, :300/:335/:428 unwrap_or(false), prepare_kernel copy :600/:670) is exactly the pattern force_no_rebar must follow. VulkanContext already holds memory_properties (:176) and non_coherent_atom_size (:200), so rebar_available can be probed once at construction.

Caller audit (Lever A byte-exactness): dispatch_saxpy.rs:151 passes output_sizes=[buf_size,buf_size] (echoes readonly X) but asserts ONLY outputs[1] (Y); dispatch.rs:170 (saxpy) reads outputs[1]; dispatch.rs:210 (vector_add, [s,s,s]) reads outputs[2]; dispatch_q4km.rs:162 ([q_len,x_len,4]) reads outputs[2]. NO caller asserts on the content of a read-only binding's readback. Lever A's change of those indices to empty Vec is BEHAVIOR-SAFE for every existing test/bench, AND directly corroborates the profiling claim that saxpy reads 8MB when only 4MB is output.
warnings: WARNING (Lever A trust boundary, NON-BLOCKING): Lever A keys readback on the access ANNOTATION (ReadOnly → never read back). If a kernel is annotated readonly_buffer but the SHADER actually writes that binding (user lies / codegen bug / aliasing), Lever A will silently NOT read back the written data and the caller gets an empty Vec instead of corrupted-but-present data — a SILENT correctness change. This is acceptable because (a) ReadOnly already emits Decoration::NonWritable (buffer.rs:13), so a shader that writes a NonWritable SSBO is ALREADY ill-formed SPIR-V that spirv-val/the driver should reject before dispatch — the annotation is enforced upstream, not merely trusted; (b) the access classification Lever A reads is the SAME one codegen used to decorate the buffer, so the runtime cannot disagree with the shader's declared capability. Recommend the Coder add a one-line comment at binding_is_readback tying the ReadOnly skip to the NonWritable decoration so the trust chain is documented. Not a revision blocker.

WARNING (non-coherent ReBAR is UNTESTED on real hardware, NON-BLOCKING, already disclosed): AT-1424 only exercises the invalidate CALL SITE structurally + on synthetic memory props; the Blackwell Type 4 is HOST_COHERENT so invalidate is a no-op on the dev box. A vendor where DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE is genuinely NON-coherent (the NVIDIA-passes/AMD-corrupts scenario) is NOT proven by any AT — it is explicitly scoped out as EB.1 (cross-vendor, M3.x). This is HONEST disclosure, not a hidden gap: the invalidate is placed AFTER the fence and BEFORE copy_out, atom-aligned via the existing mapped_range (which AT-1410 covers), and prefers the COHERENT ReBAR type when both exist. The design does the maximum it can without the hardware. Accept with the scope-out documented.

WARNING (ReBAR buffer retains TRANSFER_SRC|TRANSFER_DST + CONCURRENT, NON-BLOCKING): open_question B/4 keeps TRANSFER usage and the design keeps CONCURRENT sharing on the ReBAR output even though a pure-ReBAR output is touched only by compute + host (no transfer queue). This is SAFE (CONCURRENT is strictly more permissive; unused TRANSFER usage is legal) and reuses the single create path, but it leaves a micro-opt on the table and means the ReBAR buffer is declared CONCURRENT over a transfer family it never visits. No ownership/visibility hole: QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED on the SHADER_WRITE→HOST_READ barrier + CONCURRENT means no acquire/release is needed. Accept the default (keep).
spirv_concerns: NONE. r2 is pure host-side data movement: no codegen, no SPIR-V, no descriptor-layout, no annotation-lowering change. The ReBAR buffer is bound as the identical STORAGE_BUFFER SSBO (kernel_handle.rs:441); STORAGE_BUFFER usage is correctly flagged MANDATORY. spirv-val is unaffected (self_check confirms; verified the descriptor write site is untouched).
vendor_concerns: ReBAR ABSENCE handled correctly: Lavapipe (CI) exposes no DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE type → rebar_available=false → every buffer uses allocate_device_local_buffer (mapping=None) → byte-identical to r1. AT-1416 asserts this on synthetic props. force_no_rebar exercises the SAME fallback on ReBAR hardware (AT-1423), so the fallback's load-bearing-ness is CI-visible — good discipline mirroring r1.

iGPU unified memory: find_rebar_memory_type_index returns the unified DEVICE_LOCAL|HOST_VISIBLE type; only OUTPUT bindings get the mapped allocation, non-outputs use the plain (unmapped) allocation of the same type. No aliasing (distinct buffers). open_question 1 correctly identifies an iGPU upload micro-opt left on the table — acceptable for M3.0.
Non-coherent ReBAR (potential AMD behavior): handled by Coherency::NonCoherent + invalidate, but unproven on real hardware (see warning). Scoped to EB.1 honestly.
lever_a_judgment: RESOLVED. Predicate `output_size>0 && access!=ReadOnly` is keyed on the RIGHT classification (the same access that drives the NonWritable decoration). WriteOnly/ReadWrite still read back byte-exact (the predicate gates ONLY ReadOnly — B3 satisfied). Empty-Vec for skipped slots matches the EXISTING output_size==0 contract (readback_from_persistent_mapping:1456 already pushes Vec::new()). Caller audit confirms no test reads a read-only index. Vendor-independent. The only residual is the annotation-trust boundary, mitigated by the upstream NonWritable decoration (non-blocking warning).
lever_b_barrier_judgment: RESOLVED. The single VkBufferMemoryBarrier (src=SHADER_WRITE, dst=HOST_READ, srcStage=COMPUTE_SHADER, dstStage=HOST, QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED) on device_local.buffer is the correct and sufficient host-visibility memory-domain operation, replacing the r1 (SHADER_WRITE→TRANSFER_READ)+(copy)+(TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ) triple. The design EXPLICITLY forbids recording any device→staging cmd_copy_buffer or stale TRANSFER barrier for ReBAR outputs (handoff note 'DO NOT emit the SHADER_WRITE→TRANSFER_READ or TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ barriers'). Placed on the dispatch CB (single-queue CB or dedicated COMPUTE CB) so the fence wait observes it. No double-handling.
lever_b_coherency_judgment: RESOLVED-FOR-DEV-BOX, SCOPED-OUT-FOR-CROSS-VENDOR. Type 4 is HOST_COHERENT → invalidate no-op (correct). Non-coherent ReBAR path is specified (invalidate after fence, before copy_out, atom-aligned via mapped_range, prefer COHERENT type when both exist) and reuses persistent_map.rs verbatim, but is unproven on genuinely non-coherent hardware (AT-1424 is structural/synthetic only). Honestly disclosed as EB.1. The CODE PATH is correct by construction; only real-HW validation is deferred. Acceptable.
lever_b_submit_collapse_judgment: RESOLVED. The collapse is NOT a new branch — it reuses r1's existing signal_fence_directly (kernel_handle.rs:1329) + readback_cb_opt=None path. `has_staged_readback = any read-back binding that is non-ReBAR` strictly generalizes the existing `has_outputs` gate (when all read-back bindings are ReBAR, has_staged_readback is false ⇒ exactly the r1 no-outputs path: compute signals the fence, 3→2→1 submits). Walked the timeline values: base_val+1 (upload), base_val+2 (compute); a skipped readback leaves the compute submit signaling the fence with no readback wait-value consumed — identical to r1's no-outputs case. Error-recovery matrix (:1148-1222) already tolerates readback_cb_opt=None at every failure site. Mixed case (some ReBAR, some staged): readback CB copies only staged bindings, ReBAR barriers on the compute CB — keeps 3 submits, no new hole. No partial-failure or semaphore-value gap introduced.
lever_b_dual_mapping_lifetime_judgment: RESOLVED. DeviceLocalBuffer.mapping: Option<PersistentMapping>; unmap-before-destroy-before-free on BOTH Drop (mirrors the staging block at :189-210) and grow (:377-388), consuming the Option by value so a forgotten unmap is structurally visible. No double-unmap (Option consumed exactly once; None for non-ReBAR/plain slots). No use-after-unmap on grow (unmap precedes destroy_buffer/free_memory, the mandatory Vulkan order). Send/Sync: the second mapping is Send-only and dereferenced ONLY under the per-handle buffers Mutex — CRITICAL-6's argument extends verbatim (lib.rs note confirms). On vkMapMemory failure during rebar allocation, buffer+memory are destroyed in the same error path (mirrors allocate_staging_buffer_cached:482-492). Sound.
q4km_rescope_judgment: HONEST ENGINEERING, NOT GOALPOST-MOVING. The profiling is internally consistent and falsifiable: q4km_512's output is one f32 per row (a few bytes), so a readback-path fix (the ONLY thing r2 changes) CANNOT materially move a 5.76ms total dominated by the 2MB x-vector upload DMA + single-row matvec compute. r2 does NOT claim <2ms, does NOT re-bless q4km_512 to a passing baseline (baselines.json updates it to the MEASURED value with the gate deferred), and AT-1401/qa_handoff explicitly instruct QA to record-not-fail. Deferring the <2ms gate to M3.1 MULTI-ROW matmul is technically justified (compute amortizes the upload; a tiled kernel exists there) rather than an excuse — single-row matvec is genuinely the wrong workload for that gate. The saxpy_1m <1ms gate REMAINS the primary, measured, falsifiable proof and is NOT moved. This is the OPPOSITE of reward-hacking: r2 surfaces the miss, attributes it correctly, and refuses to claim a number it cannot hit. open_question 3 correctly routes the re-scope decision to the supervisor rather than self-approving it.
saxpy_marginal_judgment: HONEST. The design REPEATEDLY admits the projection is ~0.9–1.1ms and may be MARGINAL (1.0–1.1ms), names the exact residual (copy_in's 252µs cached upload), routes the marginal-pass decision to the supervisor (open_question 2), and instructs QA to flag MARGINAL not FAILED with the phase breakdown (qa_handoff). It does NOT pretend a clean sub-1ms pass. The performance model is arithmetically traceable (252µs copy_in + ~600µs upload-DMA+compute + ~67µs 4MB@60GB/s ReBAR read + ~31µs ≈ 0.95ms) and the ~600µs is r1's measured 750µs MINUS the readback DMA that ReBAR removes — a defensible subtraction, not a fabricated number. Credible and appropriately hedged.
acceptance_honesty_overall: AT-1421-1425 + extended AT-1418 DO prove the load-bearing paths on the dev box: AT-1422 (ReBAR bit-exact + mapping.is_some() introspection), AT-1423 (force_no_rebar fallback byte-equal + mapping.is_none()), AT-1425 (submit-collapse no-readback-CB bit-exact + has_staged_readback unit), AT-1424 (invalidate ordering structural), and the FIVE-WAY byte-exact AT-1418 (single/dedicated/non-coherent/binary/force_no_rebar vs default ReBAR) — a missing invalidate, a stale transfer barrier, or a wrong read-only-skip surfaces as byte divergence on the dev box. The ONE honest gap (genuinely non-coherent ReBAR on a real non-coherent vendor) is explicitly EB.1/out-of-scope, not hidden.
most_dangerous_hole: NONE rises to blocking. The closest-to-dangerous (and the one to watch in code review) is the Lever-A annotation-trust boundary: a binding declared readonly_buffer but written by a buggy/lying shader now silently returns an EMPTY readback instead of present-but-wrong bytes. It is NOT blocking because ReadOnly already emits Decoration::NonWritable, making such a shader ill-formed SPIR-V that spirv-val/the driver rejects upstream — so the runtime's skip cannot disagree with the shader's declared write capability. Recommend (non-blocking) a Coder comment at binding_is_readback documenting that the ReadOnly skip is safe BECAUSE of the NonWritable decoration.
summary: r2 is sound and the re-scope is honest. Both levers verified against the ACTUAL code, not just the spec: Lever A's predicate keys on the correct access classification (the same one driving NonWritable) and changes only read-only readback indices that NO existing test/bench asserts on; Lever B reuses r1's already-implemented signal_fence_directly/has_outputs collapse machinery and the proven unmap-before-destroy PersistentMapping pattern, with the SHADER_WRITE→HOST_READ(dstStage=HOST) barrier as the sole, correct readback dependency for ReBAR outputs and no leftover transfer copy/barrier. The submit collapse is a strict generalization (has_staged_readback ⊇ has_outputs), not a new failure surface. Coherency is correct-by-construction for the dev box (HOST_COHERENT Type 4) with the genuinely-non-coherent-ReBAR case honestly scoped to EB.1. The q4km_512 <2ms re-scope is justified profiling-driven honesty (readback fixes cannot move an upload+compute-bound single-row matvec) and is routed to the supervisor, not self-approved; the saxpy_1m gate stays the primary proof and is appropriately hedged as possibly-marginal. Three non-blocking warnings (annotation-trust boundary, untested non-coherent ReBAR, retained CONCURRENT/TRANSFER on ReBAR output) — all already disclosed or upstream-enforced. APPROVE.
